claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys occupy a broad compositional space containing diverse elemental mixtures.
A machine-learning approach trained on high-throughput simulation and experimental data can rapidly identify promising RHEA compositions.
The machine-learning approach can reliably identify RHEAs that are simultaneously intrinsically strong, ductile, and low in weight.
Machine-learning screening will outperform traditional thermo-kinetic and simulation-based screening methods.
Machine-learning models can predict RHEA strength, ductility, and density from high-throughput simulation and experimental datasets.
Model predictions correlate with phase stability and elemental distribution.
Phase stability and elemental distribution mediate the mechanical properties of RHEAs.
The machine-learning model can identify patterns connecting compositional variables to material properties.
Learned composition-property patterns enable prediction of alloys combining high strength, ductility, and low weight.
Machine-learning predictions can focus experimental work on promising alloy candidates.
ML-guided screening will yield RHEAs with enhanced mechanical performance relative to alloys identified through traditional thermo-kinetic simulations.
ML-guided screening will yield RHEAs with lower density than alloys identified through traditional thermo-kinetic simulations.
Traditional thermo-kinetic analysis and conventional simulations are slower than the proposed machine-learning approach.
Traditional methods are less efficient at navigating the RHEA compositional space than the proposed machine-learning approach.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning model depends on the quality and diversity of its training data.
Insufficient coverage of compositional space can prevent model predictions from translating to experimental conditions.
